court: District Court of Appeal of Florida

issues.label: Alimony entitlement and need/ability to pay
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Former Wife has need and Former Husband has ability to pay given the income disparity.

issues.label: Statutory alimony factors and findings
issues.why: Durational alimony requires findings on statutory factors including length of marriage and standard of living.

issues.label: Propriety of lump sum durational alimony
issues.why: Court must justify awarding alimony in lump sum form and its statutory basis and duration.

issues.label: Long-term marriage presumption
issues.why: A twenty-six-year marriage triggers presumptions affecting alimony type and amount.

issues.label: Marital vs. nonmarital asset classification
issues.why: The $5 million in assets and separate accounts require classification for equitable distribution.

issues.label: Equitable distribution of $5M assets
issues.why: Court must equitably distribute accumulated assets and support that distribution with findings.

issues.label: Treatment of separate and joint accounts
issues.why: Parties' commingling and separate accounts affect characterization and distribution.

issues.label: Disputed sufficiency of household contributions
issues.why: Conflicting testimony about whether $7,000 covered expenses affects credibility and financial findings.

issues.label: Child support amount and guidelines calculation
issues.why: Court must compute support under statutory guidelines using each party's income.

issues.label: Retroactive child support to separation date
issues.why: Retroactivity requires proper calculation and statutory support limited by permissible lookback.

issues.label: Credit for overage/temporary support paid
issues.why: Court must properly account for the Former Husband's overpayment against arrears.

issues.label: Cessation of contributions February 2022
issues.why: Former Husband stopping contributions while residing in home affects support and equity determinations.

issues.label: Unreimbursed child medical/extracurricular expenses
issues.why: The $13,000 spent and unpaid HSA/healthcare shares must be allocated between parties.

issues.label: Health care and HSA responsibility allocation
issues.why: Court must apportion the child's health insurance and uncovered medical costs.

issues.label: Child support duration to majority
issues.why: Court must confirm termination age and any special circumstances extending support.

issues.label: Ultimate decision-making authority award
issues.why: Granting sole ultimate decision-making requires best-interest findings under the parenting statute.

issues.label: Best interests of the child
issues.why: All child-related rulings must be grounded in statutory best-interest analysis.

issues.label: Time-sharing/parenting plan
issues.why: Decision-making authority implies a parenting plan the court must address.

issues.label: Preservation of factual-findings challenge
issues.why: Failure to file a motion for rehearing may waive appellate review of inadequate findings.

issues.label: Adequacy of written findings in judgment
issues.why: Statutes require specific findings for alimony, support, and distribution to permit review.

issues.label: Imputation of income issues
issues.why: Wife's part-time-to-full-time history may raise questions about earning capacity.

issues.label: Tax consequences of awards
issues.why: Court should consider tax effects of alimony and distribution on both parties.
